question: Which of the following is the highest navigable lake in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Titicaca**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lake Titicaca** is the highest navigable lake in the world, sitting at an elevation of approximately 3,812 meters (12,507 feet) above sea level.
 
• It is located on the border between **Peru and Bolivia** in the Andes Mountains.
 
• Lake Titicaca is also the largest lake in South America by volume of water and surface area.
 
• The lake has a rich cultural history and is considered a sacred place by the indigenous peoples living in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lake Huron** is one of the Great Lakes of North America but is not the highest navigable lake.
 
• **Lake Superior**, also part of the Great Lakes, is the largest freshwater lake by surface area but not the highest.
 
• **Lake Como** is a lake in Italy, known for its depth and scenic beauty, but it is not the highest navigable lake.
 
• Lake Titicaca is notable for its unique floating reed islands, where the Uros people live.
 
• The lake has more than 40 islands, some of which are densely populated.
